rows.what the ink shows: A second inspection of the rotated source crop confirms only an opening parenthesis, the M with two long strokes, a closing parenthesis and a comma. Blank paper separates the opening parenthesis from the page edge, with no separate l, stem or remnant before it. The existing l is therefore spurious and the marked span is removed; the surrounding (M) remains.

The K has an upright and two oblique arms. Its raised exponent is a horizontal two-lobed figure with a central crossing, matching the separate raised infinity on the L entry just above; there is no trailing alpha stem. The following parenthesized M is visible.

The cancelled marginal glyph preserves a central stem and a rounded enclosed counter on its upper right, but a broad diagonal and lower angular return cross the stem and counter. Those overlaid strokes do not permit distinguishing a Phi oval crossing the stem from an R bowl and leg.

The horizontal cancellation passes through nearly all baseline ink. A tall f survives with a small upper loop and a larger lower loop. Before it are a left curved stroke and a small rounded crossing; the alpha and composition circle cannot be separated reliably. On renewed inspection, the group to the right of f preserves a low rounded d bowl/shoulder joining a rising stem above the strike, which supports d. The following m humps remain merged with the cancellation and cannot be verified.

The word after support begins with the small open c curve and rounded o, followed by a compressed, nearly horizontal middle connection; its last letters have a hooked c-like turn and a high terminal t stroke. The full line places these strokes before the separate sur and underlined C-star. The letters are compressed but support compact.

The capital D survives as a tall upright and an outward rounded bowl. The rest of the short word lies directly under a thick horizontal deletion stroke, leaving only an indistinct low bump and terminal projection; e, u and x cannot be individually verified.

Inside the inverse-image parentheses there is a tall, looped complement sign followed by a separate small left brace, a rounded zero and a right brace. No pair of horizontal equals strokes or crossing diagonal for not-equal appears between the brace and zero. The separate sign before the braces distinguishes the complement reading.

The faint insertion begins with a tall pointed A, a low connected u, a second upstroke for t and a low re ending, supporting Autre. The next small group has a faint opening curve and a long low connection with a high terminal hook, but its letter divisions and the alleged colon are not secure. The final group before f has two tall close strokes and a low ending; the internal ou/t strokes needed for toute are not distinct enough to remove its uncertainty.

The pencil phrase begins with a descending p followed by a tall l and small u/s joins, and ends with a separate tall initial t and paired l ascenders in telle. The intervening word has a low hooked opening and a long compressed horizontal body; its internal letters and accents are not separately recoverable in the focused enlargement. The uncertainty is narrowed to that middle word.

At the cancelled position, a small upper turn and larger right-opening lower curve survive on the right, compatible with epsilon. A tall left stroke with a descending loop is crossed by two heavy rising diagonal strokes, so the complete original symbol or symbol group cannot be distinguished from the cancellation. Retain the candidate under uncertainty.

The upper pencil word starts with open c/o and a low n join. Its next prominent stroke has a low rounded bowl leading into a taller ascender, supporting d; a later upright t is followed by a compressed low ion ending. There is no separate late t/é structure as required by continuité. A final enlarged rotated view supports condition, independently of the meaning of the two margin words.

The lower pencil word has an initial tall t-like stroke, low e/c joins and a medial tall h ascender. Farther right, the conspicuous descending loop belongs to a late q followed by low u/e joins. This order supports technique; à gauche would require its g descender near the start, where none is visible. The new hypothesis was proposed by the independent reader and then compared directly with the already viewed and final enlarged ink.

A closed lower oval remains visible after Proposition 1. Dense blue diagonal strokes cover its upper half and send a thick stroke down inside the oval. The surviving outline is consistent with 0, but the cancelled upper and internal strokes prevent a secure identification of the original glyph.

Before the thick horizontal cancellation, the opening s and low ur joins remain visible. Two low rounded joins form the following un. The last word preserves several lower bowls and two raised strokes toward its end, but its centre is merged with the heavy cancellation; ensemble remains plausible without its distinguishing middle letters surviving clearly.

The first word has a q loop with a straight descender, low u joins and a dotted final i. The next word begins with a small a followed by the taller d, then low m/e joins and a pair of raised t strokes before its final e. The full visible sequence is qui admette.

Immediately after d in the final integral, the glyph has a long descending first stem, an upward shoulder and a short returning right leg. That descender and second shoulder distinguish mu from the single low v-shaped nu candidate.

notes: Only assigned marks M0065–M0072 are primary readings here. M0073, M0075, M0076 and M0078 were requested later for a separate independent check and are recorded separately.

At final reconciliation, the existing first_margin and formula_context crops were inspected again. The independent negative-ink result for M0065 agrees with my renewed view, so the spurious l is removed. The d in M0068 was also recovered from its surviving rounded bowl/shoulder and rising stem.

Cancellation still removes distinguishing strokes in M0067, the leading and final portions of M0068, and M0070. M0072 remains partly uncertain after natural and increased-contrast enlargements. No OCR or image text extraction was used.

notes.reader: GPT-6 Astra Pro; effort not exposed; run /root/audit_tools/scan007_b
notes: Primary submission covers only M0073–M0080. M0073 and M0078 were requested for independent reading. The independent reader proposed technique for M0076; direct reinspection supports that reading, and the final view supports condition at M0075. M0074 and M0077 remain uncertain after focused inspection. All crops use source pixels of the 1759 × 2597 original; rotated views record rotation in purpose. No OCR, text recognition or Hua comparison used.

reconciliations: M0065 and M0068 were re-inspected by primary a after independent b; their final readings now agree.

M0075/M0076 retain primary b medium-confidence condition/technique, supported by its explicit d-t-ion and h-q-ue observations. Independent a favors those possibilities but is less certain; that independent uncertainty remains unaltered in its report.
M0078 retains primary b clear sur un with ensemble uncertain; independent a kept the whole phrase uncertain. Both ink observations are preserved; no claim of unanimous recovery is made.
M0072 and M0073 narrowed readings agree across primary and reciprocal inspection.
